service.name: Wedding music in Vail
service.serviceType: Live music for weddings in Vail: ceremony guitarist, cocktail hour duo, band and DJ
service.description: Live wedding music in Vail and the Vail Valley: an acoustic, jazz or Spanish guitarist for an outdoor ceremony, a jazz or acoustic duo for the cocktail hour, a band or DJ for the reception, on one contract with sound included and one I-70 travel line.

faqs.q: Do you play weddings in Vail?
faqs.a: Yes, the whole day or any one part of it, at the fee a Denver wedding sees plus one travel line for the drive, with no lodging line. Every size arrives with sound, setup and pack-down, a certificate of insurance and a W-9. Signet Artists books Vail weddings from Denver.

faqs.q: What does the Vail travel line cover?
faqs.a: The drive up I-70 and back over Vail Pass for the musicians and the gear, as one line on the quote. Vail sits inside the corridor we price as a single travel line, so there's no mileage arithmetic and no night's lodging, which the far resorts like Aspen and Telluride do carry. On a winter date the musicians travel early and the venue knows it.

faqs.q: Can a band play an outdoor wedding in Vail?
faqs.a: Yes, with the village noise cap in the plan from the start. Vail's outdoor limit in the resort villages was reported at 65 dBA measured ten feet from the permitted area, which a ceremony guitarist and a cocktail hour duo sit inside on their own. A dance floor runs louder than that by design, so it goes indoors or onto a permitted terrace, and we confirm the current figure with the venue before the day.

faqs.q: How far ahead should we book wedding musicians in Vail?
faqs.a: Earlier than in the city. A mountain venue books its Saturdays twelve to eighteen months out, and couples tend to book music after the venue and before most of the rest of the list. Tell us the date and we'll come back quickly with an answer and a price.
